dimension_justifications.soundness: The core certificate statements and short proofs are readable, and the manuscript repeatedly confines claims to the turnover/calibration assumptions. I did not independently re-prove or replay the bundled evidence.
dimension_justifications.presentation: The paper has a faithful title, a clear central decision problem, clean mathematical typesetting overall, and unusually explicit scope boundaries. However, a reader must decode too many labels and evidence statuses before seeing the central hierarchy, and the nine-page flow is disrupted by late tables and visible proof-ending artifacts.
dimension_justifications.contribution: The paired regret-certificate framing, the explicit exact-versus-asymptotic frontier, and the deliberately limited width-surrogate diagnostic are distinct and potentially useful. The presentation correctly avoids turning the latter two into stronger policy claims.

paper_summary: The paper studies choosing or abstaining among fixed classifiers when subgroup mixture weights shift but within-subgroup conditional risks remain fixed. It gives absolute and paired finite-sample regret certificates, evaluates certificate-gated point-estimate selection, compares exact paired bounds with a normal/CLT diagnostic, and reports label-budget allocation experiments plus a deliberately narrower certificate-width surrogate.
strongest_verified_contribution: The clearest verified contribution in the snapshot is the paired-difference certificate presentation together with the explicit boundary that Maurer--Pontil and Hoeffding are exact finite-sample certificates, normal/CLT is only an asymptotic diagnostic, and the M3.5 allocation calculation is not an optimizer or safe rule for the actual regret UCB.
strengths: The title and abstract accurately identify the problem, decision object, finite-sample scope, and abstention boundary.
Exact certificates, the normal/CLT diagnostic, and the width-surrogate allocation analysis are repeatedly and honestly distinguished in Table 2, Sections 6--7, Limitations, and Conclusion.
Tables are numerically legible and their captions usually state tolerance, confidence level, seeds, and the descriptive status of reported outcomes.
The main nine pages maintain a consistent visual style and show no clipped text, illegible math, or anonymity issue.
questions: Can the authors add a compact early taxonomy that maps P1/P2/P3 and M1/M2/M2.5/M3/M3.5 to selection rule, certificate status, and supporting table or theorem?
Can Table 5 be moved before Section 8 or to the appendix so that Related Work is not interrupted across pages 8--9?
Can the authors expand abbreviated outcome headers in Tables 1 and 5, especially forced, abst. mean, and med. UB, or define them directly below each table?

issues.location: Abstract and Section 1.1; Sections 5--7 and Tables 1--4
issues.observed_evidence: The abstract and contribution list introduce P1/P3, M2/M2.5, M3, and M3.5 before the reader has a single mapping from these labels to their decision role and evidentiary status. Table 1 names only the M2 and asymptotic paired-normal endpoints, while Table 2 adds exact M2.5 variants; the width-surrogate material is carefully caveated later but requires substantial backtracking to distinguish it from an allocation policy.
issues.why_it_matters: The paper's central credibility depends on readers never conflating exact certificates, empirical normal diagnostics, and the non-policy width surrogate. The necessary distinctions are present, but are distributed across a dense narrative, which makes a mistaken takeaway plausible on a first read.
issues.required_fix: Add an early compact taxonomy or running-status box with rows for M1, M2, exact M2.5 variants, normal/CLT M2.5, M3, and M3.5; state selection rule, guarantee status, empirical role, and relevant theorem/table. Use the same labels in abstract and table captions.
issues.verification_test: Give a reader only the revised first two pages and taxonomy, then ask them to classify 0.260, 0.503, and M3.5 as exact finite-sample certificate, asymptotic diagnostic, or width-surrogate diagnostic. All three classifications should be correct without consulting later sections.
issues.evidence_needed: No new experiment is needed; this is an organization and labeling repair using existing claims and tables.

issues.observed_evidence: Section 8 begins at the bottom of page 8, but Table 5 from the preceding width-surrogate section is placed at the top of page 9 before the continuation of the first Related Work paragraph. The resulting sequence is surrogate table/caption, then the interrupted Saerens sentence, then remaining related-work paragraphs. The paper also has no main-text visual showing the FIT/CAL/test decision-and-certificate pipeline or three evidentiary layers.
issues.why_it_matters: This break harms the nine-page argument flow precisely where the reader needs to consolidate what is a theorem, an observed certificate outcome, and an allocation diagnostic.
issues.required_fix: Reflow or defer Table 5 so every Section 8 paragraph is contiguous; use recovered space to add one compact pipeline/status figure or table, or move secondary M3.5 detail to the appendix while retaining its scope statement in main text.
issues.verification_test: Render the revised nine-page main text and confirm that Related Work is contiguous, each retained table occurs after its first substantive callout without crossing a section boundary, and a reader can trace FIT allocation, CAL certification, and held-out test settlement from one visual or compact table.

issues.location: Proof endings on pages 3--4 and Provision 1 typo
issues.observed_evidence: Rendered proofs show duplicate square/QED markers; Proposition 3 shows a square in its statement as well as proof-ending squares. The closing paired-cancellation sentence says Provision 1 rather than Proposition 1.
issues.why_it_matters: These visible artifacts create unnecessary ambiguity about where proofs end and reduce confidence in otherwise concise theorem presentation.
issues.required_fix: Remove redundant manually inserted QED markers from proof environments, remove the QED from the Proposition 3 statement, and correct Provision to Proposition.
issues.verification_test: Recompile and visually inspect pages 3--4: each proof has exactly one terminal marker, no proposition statement has a proof-ending marker, and a text search returns no occurrence of Provision 1.

issues.observed_evidence: Table 1 uses terse headers comm. mean/max, abst. mean, and forced, while Table 5 uses commit and med. UB. Captions provide partial context, but a reader cannot immediately tell the denominator or precise quantity for every abbreviated column without reading surrounding prose.
issues.why_it_matters: These are the main numerical interfaces for comparing exact/asymptotic endpoints and allocation diagnostics; self-contained labels reduce misinterpretation.
issues.required_fix: Expand abbreviations or add a one-line legend beneath each table defining every outcome, its unit/aggregation, and whether it is an observed test diagnostic or certificate property.
issues.verification_test: A reader can define every numeric column using only each revised table and caption.

ethics_concerns: No direct ethics issue is apparent. The paper appropriately states that fallback utility, latency, and monetary costs are unmeasured rather than claiming operational benefit.
llm_usage_disclosure: This review was produced by an isolated AI subagent for internal pre-submission quality control.
evidence_that_would_raise_score: A revised nine-page PDF that passes taxonomy, layout, table-legibility, and proof-artifact verification tests without weakening exact/asymptotic/surrogate boundaries.
A comprehension check showing that the three evidentiary categories can be correctly identified from the early paper presentation.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: Any revised wording or table that treats normal/CLT as finite-sample support.
Any revision presenting M3.5 as an optimizer, safe allocation rule, or deployment policy for the actual regret UCB.
A reflow that exceeds the nine-page main-text limit or further separates tables from interpretation.
review_limitations: I reviewed only the frozen snapshot and did not independently replay experiments or verify external literature.
